root_idea.summary: Swift, deft taking up or catching of something.
root_idea.development: The lexical range connects skilled taking by the mouth or hand with the Quranic sense of swallowing up, and with the derived Form V sense of catching and retaining speech quickly.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form لَقِفَ rather than the imperfect Quranic lemma تَلْقَفُ.

senses.definition: To take up swiftly and deftly; in the Quranic construction, to swallow or engulf what is taken in.
senses.usage_conditions: The action is described as skilled taking whether by mouth or hand, while the supplied Quranic occurrences use the mouth-oriented sense of swallowing up.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To catch and retain something quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V transitive construction; the attested example applies the action to words caught from another's mouth.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The swift, deft taking-up meaning is represented in the Quranic sense.
The Form V catching-and-retaining construction is represented as a Classical meaning.

cautions: The QAC group contains imperfect active Form I occurrences; the public headword is normalized to the perfect citation form لَقِفَ.
